\begin{definition}[Initial register state]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.mk}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.mk}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg}
Given natural numbers $n,\ell,S,K,i,cnt,c,d,j$, define a register state with input
length $n$, parameter $\ell$, radius $S$, exponent $0$, parameter $K$, run count $K+1$,
runs remaining $i$, accepting-run count $cnt$, current code $c$, candidate code $d$, and
coins remaining $j$; all four scratch values are zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Probabilistic semantics of a copy operation]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.ps_cp}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.ps_cp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.of_reach, Complexity.LogProg.copy_run, Randomized.PolyAmp.CpS, Randomized.PolyAmp.Lab, Randomized.PolyAmp.PS, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.Le, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.le_v, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.v, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampA, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr, Randomized.PolyAmp.cpDst, Randomized.PolyAmp.cpEx, Randomized.PolyAmp.cpSrc}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $os$ be a Boolean, let $x$ be a
Boolean word, and let $B$ be a natural number. For a copy type $k$, let
$r_{\mathrm{src}}(k)$ and $r_{\mathrm{dst}}(k)$ denote its source and destination
register indices, and let $q_k$ be its exit label. Suppose a register state $\sigma$ has
every register at most $B$, its scratch value $z$ is zero, and the sum of its source and
destination register values is at most $B$. Suppose also that $\sigma'$ has register
vector obtained from that of $\sigma$ by replacing the destination value with the sum of
the source and destination values. If the configuration at label $q_k$ with register
state $\sigma'$ has probabilistic semantics with probability $p$, then the configuration
at the initial copy label for $k$ with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic
semantics with probability $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Initial configuration code test]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_init}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_init}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr, Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_initLang_iff, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, Boolean input word $x$, and
natural numbers $S,c$, the Boolean indicator of the initialization language, evaluated
on the encoding of $x$ together with the binary representations of $c$ and $S$, equals
true exactly when $c$ is the code of the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ using
window size $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step configuration code test]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_step}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr, Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_stepLang_iff, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, $x$ a Boolean input word, and $S$ a
natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(|x|)$ space on every choice word for some
function $sp$, and $sp(|x|)\le S$. If $C$ is reachable from the initial configuration of
$N$ on $x$, then for every natural number $c'$, the Boolean indicator of the one-step
language on the encoding of $x$, the code of $C$ with window size $S$, the number $c'$,
and $S$ equals true exactly when $c'$ is the code, with window size $S$, of one of the
two configurations obtained from $C$ by a step under a choice bit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance test for reachable configurations]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_accept}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_accept}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr, Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_acceptLang_iff, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Booleans, let $x$ be a
Boolean input, and let $S\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose there is a function
$sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every run of $N$ on every Boolean input $y$ under
every choice word uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells, and suppose $sp(|x|)\le S$. If
$C$ is a configuration whose core data and output summary agree with those of some
configuration reached by running $N$ from its initial configuration on $x$ under a
choice word, then the Boolean indicator of the acceptance-configuration language,
evaluated on the encoding of $x$, the code of $C$ at space bound $S$, and $S$, is true
exactly when $C$ is halted with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.mk_le}

\leanok

\difficulty{2}
Let $n,\ell,S,K,i,\mathrm{cnt},c,d,j,B$ be natural numbers. Suppose $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le
B$, $i\le K+1$, $\mathrm{cnt}\le K+1$, and $c,d,j\le K$. Then the register state
initialized with these values has every register at most $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Sampling-loop probability]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.ps_steps}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.ps_steps}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.choose, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.dec, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.of_reach, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.searchDown_run, Complexity.LogProg.searchUp_run, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₂, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₃, Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.PolyAmp.Lab, Randomized.PolyAmp.PS, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.step, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.Le, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.le_v, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.u_10, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.u_7, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.u_8, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.u_9, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.v, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.v_2, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.v_7, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reg.v_8, Randomized.PolyAmp.accP, Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_succ, Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_zero, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampA, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_accept, Randomized.PolyAmp.ampOr_step, Randomized.PolyAmp.cfgCode_lt_codeBound, Randomized.PolyAmp.codeBound, Randomized.PolyAmp.cpDst, Randomized.PolyAmp.cpSrc, Randomized.PolyAmp.mk, Randomized.PolyAmp.mk_le, Randomized.PolyAmp.ps_cp, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let
$sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and fix a Boolean input $x$. Suppose $N$ uses at most
$sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells on every input $y$ and every choice word, $sp(|x|)\le S$, the
configuration-code bound for $N$, $|x|$, and $S$ is at most $K$, and $n+\ell+S+2K+2\le
B$. Let $i,cnt\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $i\le K+1$ and $cnt+1\le K+1$, and let
$A_1,A_0\in\mathbb{Q}$ be such that for every $c,d\le K$, the run-loop configurations
with accepting-run counts $cnt+1$ and $cnt$, respectively, have probabilities $A_1$ and
$A_0$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, every configuration $C$ on input $x$ reachable
from the initial configuration in the sense that its machine state, input-head position,
work-tape contents and head positions, and output summary agree with those of a
configuration reached by some choice word, and every $d\le K$, the sampling-loop
configuration initialized with the code of $C$ has probability $\Pr[\text{accepting
after }j\text{ random choice bits}]A_1+(1-\Pr[\text{accepting after }j\text{ random
choice bits}])A_0$, where the probability is taken over uniformly random choice words of
length $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance bit]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accBit}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accBit}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet and Boolean
lists $x$ and $l$, the acceptance bit is true exactly when $N$ accepts input $x$ using
choice sequence $l$; otherwise it is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decision rule]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.decRule}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.decRule}
\leanok
For a Boolean $os$ and natural numbers $K,m$, the decision bit is true exactly when
$1\le m$ if $os$ is true, and exactly when $K+1<2m$ if $os$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Run acceptance probability]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.accBit, Randomized.PolyAmp.decRule, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet, a Boolean
input $x$, a Boolean $os$, and natural numbers $K,i,cnt$, the run value is the
probability, over $iK$ uniformly random bits, that the decision rule with parameters
$os,K$ accepts the sum of $cnt$ and the number of accepting blocks among the $i$ blocks
of $K$ bits, where a block is accepting when $N$ accepts $x$ using that block as its
choice sequence.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Run Value at Zero Blocks]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal_zero}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.decRule, Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$
be a Boolean input, and let $K,c$ be nonnegative integers. With zero blocks, the run
value starting at count $c$ is $1$ if the decision rule applied to $c$ returns true, and
is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.runVal_succ}

\leanok

\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output
alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $K,i,c$ be nonnegative integers. The run
value for $i+1$ blocks, starting with count $c$, equals $p$ times the run value for $i$
blocks starting with count $c+1$, plus $(1-p)$ times the run value for $i$ blocks
starting with count $c$, where $p$ is the probability that $N$ accepts on a uniformly
random choice word of length $K$ when run on $x$.
\end{theorem}

Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be
a Boolean input word, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ bound the space used by $N$
on every input and every choice word. Let $n,\ell,S,K,B\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $os$ be a

B$. For every $i,cnt,c,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $cnt+i\le K+1$, $c\le K$, and $d\le K$, the

$(n,\ell,S,K,i,cnt,c,d,0)$ terminates for every sequence of choice bits, keeps each
